newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX oil prices called lower on bearish APIs.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX oil prices called lower on bearish APIs.

text.p: NYMEX oil prices were called lower Wednesday after weekly oil inventory data showed a surprising build in gasoline stocks when traders had expected a decline, indicating poor gasoline demand.

"The data was a surprise because people were looking for seasonal demand for gasoline and they are not getting it which is a disappointment," said Victor Yu, vice president of Refco Inc. Gasoline demand begins to rise in the spring and typically climaxes during the summer driving season.
Crude was called 20 to 25 cents a barrel lower while refined products were called off 0.50 to 0.75 cent a gallon.
The American Petroleum Institute's (API) oil stock data released Tuesday evening for the week ended April 11 defied traders' expectations for the entire oil complex.

Gasoline stocks swelled 3.63 million barrels compared with a one to two million barrel decline expected by traders. Implied demand fell to a seasonally weak 7.3 million barrels per day (bpd) compared with 8.1 million bpd the week before.
Crude stocks rose 2.97 million barrels for the week ended April 11 compared with a one million barrel build anticipated by traders. This is the sixth consecutive weekly crude stock build.
Crude stocks are now 11.3 million barrels higher than a year ago in the U.S. Gulf where refinery demand is concentrated.

Despite unseasonably cold weather in the key heating oil market of the U.S. Northeast, distillate stocks grew 2.59 million barrels when traders expected a decline of 1.5 million barrels. Distillate stocks include heating oil and diesel.
Dealers said the market is also technically weak after spot crude failed for the second time this week to close above $20.00 after rising above that level on Monday for the first time in two weeks.
"We are now rangebound again," said a trader, referring to the $19.00 to $20.00 range spot crude has languished in since April 2.

On Tuesday, May crude ended seven cents a barrel lower at $19.83 after rising as high as $20.09. May gasoline ended 0.06 cent a gallon lower at 61.90 cents a gallon while May heating oil ended up 0.18 cent a gallon at 54.85 cents.
-- Harry Milling, New York Energy Desk, 212-859-1761
